commonName: Alternaria leaf spot (black spot / leaf blight)
pathogen: Alternaria brassicae (Berkeley) Saccardo; Alternaria brassicicola is also reported on cole crops
symptoms: Small dark spots appear first on the older, lower leaves. Each spot becomes round and is about 1 mm across to begin with, then widens and shows dark rings inside it, one inside the other like a target, often with a yellow halo around the edge. In humid weather or persistent dew a sooty dark growth forms in the middle of the spot. As spots keep enlarging they run together and whole leaves dry up and blight. Narrow dark streaks also appear on the leaf stalks and stems, and dark spots spoil the green head after it has formed. Seed from affected plants is shrivelled and germinates poorly.

favorableConditions.rainfall: Soil temperature of around 28°C, high humidity or persistent dew, and moist weather with intermittent showers. The fungus survives as mycelium in the seed, as spores on the seed and in crop debris, and then spreads by wind-borne or insect-borne spores.

organicControl: Hot water seed treatment at 50°C for 30 minutes before sowing (National Horticulture Board advice for leaf spot and blight of cole crops)

Apply Trichoderma viride or Trichoderma harzianum and Pseudomonas fluorescens as a seed treatment, a nursery treatment and a soil application at sowing/transplanting (DPPQS/NIPHM broccoli IPM package)
Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride at 3-4 g per kg of seed (National Horticulture Board rate for cole crop seed treatment; TNAU gives 4 g per kg of seed for cabbage) to cut down seed-borne fungus

chemicalControl.dose: 0.25% foliar spray (0.25% is 2.5 g of commercial Mancozeb 75% WP per litre of water), repeated at about one month interval - TNAU Agritech recommendation for black spot (Alternaria) of cabbage and cauliflower. Note: the tridemorph listed alongside mancozeb on that TNAU page is banned for manufacture, import and use in India (S.O. 3951(E) dated 8 August 2018) and must not be used. Mancozeb itself is restricted only on guava, jowar and tapioca, so it may be used on cole crops.

0.5% spray. The National Horticulture Board gives this (or Captan 0.2%) for cole crops grown as a SEED crop, sprayed at full bloom, pod set and pre-harvest stage. It is not given there as a spray for a head crop, so check with your KVK or State Agriculture Department before using it on a broccoli head crop.

preventive: Use disease-free certified seed - the fungus is carried in and on the seed
Rotate for 3 years with crops that are not cruciferous, and remove cruciferous weeds such as wild mustard
Prune off the diseased lower leaves and burn them; collect and destroy crop debris after harvest
Allow good aeration - wide spacing, rows parallel to the prevailing wind, and not planted tight against hedgerows
Give adequate drainage to avoid excessive soil moisture, and avoid low-lying land for this crop
Grow resistant or tolerant varieties recommended by your ICAR institute, KVK or State Agricultural University

symptoms: Start by looking at the edge of the leaf. Pale yellow wedge-shaped or 'V' shaped patches begin at the leaf margin and spread inward towards the midrib; they later turn brown and then black, and that part of the leaf edge dies. Inside the patch the veins and small veinlets turn brown and then black, and the blackening runs on along the midrib into the leaf stalk and stem - if you cut the stem across, you see a black ring where the veins are. A sticky bacterial ooze can sometimes be seen on affected parts. Seedlings and young plants infected early turn yellow, shed their lower leaves, wilt and die, and often only one side of the plant is affected. Plants infected late make small, poor-quality heads that are unfit for market and may go on to rot soft and foul-smelling. Plants grown from infected seed can look healthy for several weeks before symptoms show.

favorableConditions.rainfall: Relative humidity above 90%, high soil moisture and frequent rains. The bacteria are carried inside the seed and in soil, and then spread from plant to plant in irrigation water and rain splash. Common in warm, wet weather.

organicControl: Treat the seed in hot water at 58°C for 30 minutes before sowing - this is the measure the Government of India broccoli IPM package lists against black rot

Apply Trichoderma viride or Trichoderma harzianum and Pseudomonas fluorescens as a seed treatment, a nursery treatment and a soil application at sowing/transplanting (DPPQS/NIPHM broccoli IPM package); if you buy a ready-made product, check that it carries a label claim

chemicalControl.dose: 10.0 to 12.5 kg per hectare (TNAU Agritech recommendation for black rot of cabbage)
Consult your local KVK or State Agriculture Department for the current recommended dose

preventive: Do not use streptocycline or any streptomycin + tetracycline product, which older Indian advisories still recommend for black rot: it has been prohibited in Indian agriculture since 1 January 2024.
Use disease-free certified seed and disease-free transplants - the bacteria travel inside the seed
Grow black rot tolerant or resistant varieties; ask your ICAR institute, KVK or State Agricultural University which ones are recommended locally
Keep strict crop sanitation - pull out and destroy affected plants as soon as you spot the V-shaped margin patches
Plant on raised beds and keep a proper drainage system so water does not carry the bacteria from plant to plant
Do not plant where crucifers (cabbage, cauliflower, broccoli, knol-khol, radish, mustard) have been grown in the last 2 years
Avoid splashing irrigation and avoid handling or working in the crop while the leaves are wet

symptoms: A healthy broccoli leaf is large, thick and blue-green to grey-green with a slight waxy bloom on the surface, a broad pale midrib and clear pale veins running out from it. The leaf edge is smooth and firm, with no pale yellow wedge or V-shaped patches running in from the margin. The veins are green or whitish and never brown or black. There are no dark spots with rings inside them, no sooty growth, no yellowing between the veins, and the leaf does not wilt in the day. The central head is tight, dark green and evenly beaded, with no sunken or blackened patches.
preventive: Walk through the field at least once a week and turn over the lower, older leaves - both black rot and Alternaria leaf spot start on the oldest leaves and at the leaf margins
Use disease-free certified seed and healthy transplants; both main broccoli leaf diseases are carried inside the seed
Grow resistant or tolerant varieties - ask your ICAR institute, KVK or State Agricultural University which ones suit your area (DPPQS/NIPHM broccoli IPM package)
Keep crop sanitation: collect and destroy diseased leaves and crop debris instead of leaving them in the field
Plant on raised beds with proper drainage and avoid water stagnation, so bacteria cannot move from plant to plant in standing water
Rotate for 3 years with non-cruciferous crops and pull out cruciferous weeds such as wild mustard
Keep spacing wide and rows parallel to the prevailing wind so the leaves dry quickly after rain or dew
Check the crop most carefully in humid, dewy or showery spells - that is when both diseases spread fastest

symptoms: Small brown to black spots appear on the leaves, leaf stalks and stem. They are circular to slightly elongated and often show faint rings inside, like a target. Spots join together into large dead patches and the oldest, lowest leaves go first. On a mature crop the spots carry on into the head, and in a seed crop they damage the pods. In damp weather a dark sooty growth of spores can be seen on the spot.

favorableConditions.rainfall: Warm wet weather with long leaf wetness from rain, dew or overhead irrigation. Dense planting that keeps the canopy damp makes it worse.

organicControl: Use certified disease-free seed; the fungus is carried on and in the seed
Hot water seed treatment at 50°C for 20-30 minutes before sowing
Treat seed with Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens before sowing
Remove and destroy infected lower leaves and all crop residue after harvest
Three-year rotation away from all cole crops and mustard, and control cruciferous weeds

chemicalControl.dose: 0.1% foliar spray, applied first (TNAU Agritech, cabbage black spot)
0.25% foliar spray (2.5 g of Mancozeb 75% WP per litre of water), applied a month after the first spray (TNAU Agritech, cabbage black spot)

preventive: Space plants so the canopy dries quickly, and irrigate at the base rather than overhead
Start scouting the oldest leaves from three weeks after transplanting
Do not work in the field while the foliage is wet; spores move on hands and clothes
Harvest and remove residue promptly rather than leaving it to rot in the field

pathogen: Pieris brassicae (large white cabbage butterfly); Pieris rapae also causes the same damage
symptoms: Leaves are eaten into large irregular holes, and in a heavy attack only the veins and midrib are left. The damage is chewing damage, not spotting: edges are ragged and torn, with no ring or halo. Look on the underside for clusters of upright yellow eggs, and for velvety caterpillars - pale yellow-green with black spots and a yellow stripe down the back - feeding in groups. Dark green pellets of droppings collect in the leaf axils and inside the head. Older caterpillars bore into the head itself, which spoils it for market even when the outer leaves look fine.

favorableConditions.rainfall: Mild winter and spring weather in the plains and the whole season in the hills. Numbers build on a continuous supply of cole crops, so staggered plantings next to each other keep the pest going.

organicControl: Collect and destroy the caterpillars and egg clusters in the early stage of attack, before they reach the head (TNAU)
Conserve the parasitoid Cotesia glomeratus, which attacks the caterpillars naturally; avoid broad-spectrum sprays that kill it (TNAU)
Spray Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki, which kills caterpillars and spares the parasitoids and bees
Spray neem seed kernel extract 5%, or azadirachtin 5% at 5.0 ml per 10 litres of water, which TNAU gives for the diamondback moth on the same crop
Set up light traps at 1 per hectare to catch the adults, and grow a mustard trap crop around the field

chemicalControl.dose: TNAU gives 1000 ml for cabbage butterfly without stating the spray volume, so confirm the per-litre dilution and the pre-harvest interval on the product label with your local KVK before spraying. Use it only if hand collection and Bacillus thuringiensis have not held the pest, and never on a crop close to harvest.

preventive: Inspect the undersides of leaves weekly and crush egg clusters, which is faster than spraying later
Do not plant a new cole crop next to one that is already infested
Plough and remove residue after harvest so pupae do not carry over
Spray only when caterpillars are small; large ones inside the head cannot be reached

symptoms: Soft, water-soaked brown or grey patches appear on the leaf, usually starting at a wound, a bruise or an old dying leaf rather than in the middle of healthy tissue. In damp weather the patch is covered with a grey, fuzzy coat of mould that puffs up in a cloud if you touch it. The rot is soft and mushy, not dry and papery. Hard black bodies the size of a grain may form under the rotted part later. It spreads fastest on leaves already damaged by caterpillars, hail or frost, and on heads in storage.

favorableConditions.rainfall: Cool damp weather with high humidity and poor air movement. It takes hold on plant debris and weak tissue - old flowers, dying lower leaves, bruised or overripe produce - rather than on healthy growing leaves.

organicControl: Remove and destroy dying lower leaves, fallen debris and infected plant material promptly, which is the main control
Avoid overhead watering and wetting the foliage; the fungus spreads in splashing water and wind
Space plants widely and avoid overcrowding, since grey mould thrives in shaded, crowded plantings
Handle heads carefully at harvest: almost every infection starts at a bruise or a cut
Copper fungicides and neem oil are permitted organic options, though neem is a weak fungicide against this pathogen

chemicalControl.activeIngredient: Fungicide registered for Botrytis on cole crops
chemicalControl.dose: Consult your local KVK or State Agriculture Department for the current recommended dose. No Indian extension source giving a dose for grey mould specifically on cabbage could be confirmed, so none is stated here rather than carrying one across from another crop.

preventive: Keep the crop growing steadily; stressed, aging and frost-damaged tissue is what the fungus colonises first
Do not leave harvested heads lying in a damp heap in the field
Rotate fungicide groups if you do spray, because Botrytis develops resistance quickly
Improve drainage and avoid irrigating late in the day so the canopy is dry by nightfall

symptoms: A healthy cabbage leaf is broad, thick and smooth with a pale waxy bloom, blue-green to grey-green, with a stout white midrib and clear veins spreading from it. The margin is entire and firm, not browned, scorched or papery. There are no brown to black circular spots with rings inside them, no grey fuzzy mould, no large chewed holes between the veins, and no clusters of yellow eggs or green caterpillars on the underside. The head, if formed, is tight and firm with clean wrapper leaves.
preventive: Raise seedlings in a clean nursery bed and reject any with spots or chewed leaves at transplanting
Turn the leaves over once a week and look at the undersides, where caterpillars and eggs sit
Keep irrigation steady and avoid both water stress and waterlogging
Follow a three-year rotation away from cabbage, cauliflower, broccoli, turnip and mustard
Avoid overhead irrigation late in the day so the foliage is not wet overnight

pathogen: Not a disease and not catching. A physiological disorder: the plant cannot move enough calcium to the young inner leaves fast enough, so their margins die. High fertility, high temperatures, water stress followed by rapid growth, low humidity, and an imbalance between nitrogen, potassium and calcium all bring it on.
symptoms: The margins of the leaves scorch and die, turning brown or black and going papery and brittle. The line between dead and living tissue is sharp. Crucially it is the inner leaves that are affected, so a head can look perfectly sound from the outside and be brown along the leaf edges when it is cut open. There is no mould, no spot with a ring, no soft rot and no spore growth, and it does not spread from plant to plant - neighbouring plants are affected because they share the same soil and weather, not because of infection.

favorableConditions.rainfall: Hot weather with low humidity, and a dry spell followed by heavy irrigation or rain that pushes sudden fast growth. Heavy nitrogen or potassium makes it worse by competing with calcium uptake.

organicControl: Irrigate evenly and often enough that the crop never swings between water stress and a growth flush, which is what interrupts calcium movement
Hold nitrogen down to what the crop actually needs and prefer nitrate forms over ammonium
Avoid excess potassium and other nutrients that compete with calcium uptake
Get the soil tested and correct calcium and base saturation before planting rather than after symptoms appear
Harvest at proper maturity instead of leaving heads to become over-firm
Grow varieties known locally to be less prone; susceptibility differs widely between varieties
preventive: No spray cures it: a calcium spray reaches the outer leaves, and the damage is on the inner ones
Mulch to keep soil moisture and temperature even
Do not apply a heavy dose of nitrogen just before heading
If it appears every season on the same field, treat it as a soil and irrigation problem, not a spray problem

symptoms: A healthy garlic leaf is a long flat strap, folded along the middle, evenly blue-green to grey-green from base to tip, standing firm and upright out of the false stem. The very tip is still green and pointed, not white, straw-coloured, brown or papery. There are no yellow or orange flecks or streaks in the middle of the leaf, no spindle-shaped spots with a pink edge, no silvery-white rubbed patches, and the leaf is not twisted, curled or flattened. Pull a plant up and the roots are white and firm, with no pink colour, no rot at the base of the bulb and no white fluffy growth.
preventive: Plant big, healthy cloves over 1.5 g and reject small, diseased or damaged cloves
Plant in well-drained fertile loamy soil of pH 6-8; garlic is sensitive to highly acidic, alkali and saline soils and to waterlogging
Get the soil tested before planting and apply nutrients to the test recommendation instead of guessing
Irrigate immediately after planting and then at 7-10 day intervals; the crop is very sensitive to moisture stress at bulb initiation and bulb development, and excess irrigation is always harmful
Stop irrigation when the crop reaches maturity, 10-15 days before harvest
Walk the field weekly from 30 days after planting, checking leaf tips and both leaf surfaces for flecks, streaks, silvering or drying
Collect and burn crop residues and follow long rotations with non-host crops
Use only chemicals with a CIB&RC label claim for garlic and follow the dose and pre-harvest interval on the label

names.hi: पत्ती की नोक का झुलसना (टिप बर्न)

pathogen: No single cause - tip burn is a symptom, not one disease. Indian extension material (NIPHM / Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine & Storage) records tip burn in garlic under potassium deficiency, phosphorus deficiency and manganese deficiency. Agronomic causes are moisture stress and salinity: garlic is very sensitive to moisture stress at bulb initiation and development and to saline soil, with yield falling once saturation-extract EC crosses 3.9 dS/m (ICAR-DOGR). Pathogens can produce the same look - Stemphylium vesicarium (Stemphylium blight; spots progress from the tip to the base of the leaf), Sclerotium cepivorum (white rot; yellowing and dying back of leaf tips), Fusarium basal rot (leaves dry from tip downwards) and Pyrenochaeta terrestris (pink root; tip burn and die back). Identify the cause before spraying.
symptoms: The tip of the long flat leaf dries up and the dead area creeps downwards. It starts as a pale yellow or straw-coloured patch at the very point of the leaf, then turns white, light brown or papery and brittle, usually 1-5 cm down the leaf but sometimes much more. The line between dead and green tissue is fairly sharp. Older, outer leaves go first. Then check for the extra clues that tell you why: small yellow to orange flecks or streaks in the middle of the leaf that grow into spindle-shaped spots with a pinkish margin mean Stemphylium blight; leaves dark green and erect with older leaves turning yellow and dead mean potassium is short; light-coloured curling leaves with delayed bulbing and thick necks mean manganese is short; light green leaves with slow growth mean phosphorus is short. Now pull up two or three affected plants - pink or reddish roots, a rotting bulb base, or white fluffy growth carrying black bodies the size of mustard grains all mean the trouble is in the root or bulb and no leaf spray will fix it.

favorableConditions.rainfall: Tip burn from stress worsens in hot dry windy spells, with irregular irrigation, in saline soil or saline irrigation water, and where potassium, phosphorus or manganese is short. Where Stemphylium blight is the cause instead, warm humid weather of 18-25 C with leaves staying wet 16 hours or more favours it, and waterlogging brings on basal rot and purple blotch. The temperature and leaf wetness figures here apply to the Stemphylium cause only, not to the nutrient or moisture causes.

organicControl: If leaves are dark green and erect with older leaves yellowing, correct potassium: foliar application of K2SO4 @ 1% twice at weekly interval
If leaf tips are light coloured and curling with delayed bulbing and thick necks, correct manganese: foliar spray of MnSO4 @ 0.3% twice at fortnightly interval
If older leaves show tip burn with light green colour and slow growth, correct phosphorus: foliar spray of DAP 2% twice at fortnightly intervals
Soak garlic seed cloves in hot water at 50 C for 20 minutes before planting to cut carry-over of Stemphylium blight and purple blotch
Apply Trichoderma spp. and Pseudomonas fluorescens as clove, bulb and planting-material treatment and as soil application (check the label claim if you buy a commercial product)
Add well rotten FYM @ 10 t/acre or vermicompost @ 4 t/acre at field preparation to hold moisture and nutrients more evenly
Field sanitation - collect and burn crop residues, follow long rotations with non-host crops, keep field drainage good and reduce plant density
Keep irrigation even at 7-10 day intervals so the crop never goes through moisture stress at bulb initiation and bulb development, and never waterlog it

chemicalControl.dose: Spray @ 0.25% (0.25% works out to 2.5 g per litre of water) at 10-15 days interval from 30 days after planting or as soon as the disease appears - ICAR-DOGR recommendation for Stemphylium blight of garlic Note: only if Stemphylium blight is confirmed as the cause

Spray @ 0.1% (0.1% works out to 1 ml per litre of water) at 10-15 days interval from 30 days after planting or as soon as the disease appears - ICAR-DOGR recommendation for Stemphylium blight of garlic Note: only if Stemphylium blight is confirmed as the cause

Spray @ 0.1% (0.1% works out to 1 ml per litre of water) at 10-15 days interval from 30 days after planting or as soon as the disease appears - ICAR-DOGR recommendation for Stemphylium blight of garlic Note: only if Stemphylium blight is confirmed as the cause

Spray @ 0.1% (0.1% works out to 1 g per litre of water for a wettable powder) at 10-15 days interval from 30 days after planting or as soon as the disease appears - ICAR-DOGR recommendation for Stemphylium blight of garlic Note: only if Stemphylium blight is confirmed as the cause

chemicalControl.activeIngredient: Carbendazim (only if white rot is confirmed as the cause)
chemicalControl.dose: @ 0.1% (0.1% works out to 1 g per litre of water) applied to the soil around affected plants - ICAR-DOGR states carbendazim @ 0.1% may be applied for white rot, alongside crop rotation, destroying infected plants and soil solarization

preventive: Soil test before planting and apply to the recommendation; ICAR-DOGR advises 75:40:40:40 kg NPKS/ha for most of India and 100:50:50:50 kg NPKS + 20 t FYM/ha for Haryana, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh
Apply one third of the nitrogen and the full recommended phosphorus, potassium and sulphur as basal at planting, and the remaining nitrogen in two equal splits at 30 and 45 days after planting
Apply 30 kg sulphur/ha where soil sulphur is below 25 kg/ha, ZnSO4 @ 10 kg/ha as basal for zinc deficiency and borax @ 10 kg/ha for boron deficiency
Plant in well-drained loamy soil of pH 6-8 and avoid saline land and saline irrigation water - garlic yield starts declining once saturation-extract EC crosses 3.9 dS/m
Irrigate at 7-10 day intervals and never let the crop go through moisture stress at bulb initiation and bulb development; excess irrigation is also harmful
Reject small, diseased or damaged cloves and plant big cloves over 1.5 g
Collect and burn crop residues, follow long rotations with non-host crops and keep plant density moderate so leaves dry faster

Pull up two or three affected plants and check roots and bulb base before deciding to spray - tip burn with pink roots, a rotting bulb or white fluffy growth is a root or bulb problem that a leaf fungicide will not fix
Ask your local KVK or State Agriculture Department to confirm the cause if the nutrient corrections and better irrigation do not stop the tips drying

symptoms: Irregular reddish-brown to tan spots appear on young leaves, often with tiny black dots inside. Small, elliptical dark cankers can form on young shoots and tendrils. Berries get a black scab, then shrivel into hard black mummies.

favorableConditions.rainfall: Warm, moist climate with extended periods of rain and cloudy weather.

organicControl: Apply Trichoderma viride/harzianum and Pseudomonas fluorescens to the cuttings/planting material and as a soil application (NIPHM grapes IPM package)

chemicalControl.activeIngredient: Fungicide for grape black rot (no product has a CIB&RC label claim for this disease on grape in the ICAR-NRCG 2026-27 list)
chemicalControl.dose: Consult local KVK or agriculture officer for dosage

preventive: Remove and destroy mummified berries, infected leaves and canes, since the fungus survives in plant debris
Keep the canopy open for good air movement and faster drying
Inspect young shoots, leaves and berries closely during rainy, cloudy spells

pathogen: Fungal trunk-disease complex including Phaeomoniella chlamydospora and Phaeoacremonium spp. (e.g. P. aleophilum)
symptoms: Leaves show 'tiger-stripe' patterns: yellow (white varieties) or dark red (red varieties) stripes between the veins, with the tissue drying. Affected leaves may dry completely and drop early. Berries can show small dark spots ringed brown-purple, and may crack and dry.

favorableConditions.rainfall: Spores released during rain infect fresh pruning wounds, which stay susceptible for several weeks after pruning.

organicControl: Apply Trichoderma viride/harzianum and Pseudomonas fluorescens to the cuttings/planting material and as a soil application (NIPHM grapes IPM package)
Prune only in dry weather and protect large pruning wounds; cut out and burn dead wood, since the fungi live in the wood and no spray reaches them (NIPHM grapes IPM package)

chemicalControl.activeIngredient: Pruning-wound protectant (no product has a CIB&RC label claim for esca on grape in the ICAR-NRCG 2026-27 list; fungicides cannot eradicate established infections)
chemicalControl.dose: Consult local KVK or agriculture officer for dosage

preventive: Protect pruning wounds and avoid pruning just before or during rain
Remove and destroy dead or infected wood and heavily affected vines
Mark vines that show tiger-stripe symptoms and check them every season
Use clean planting material; infections start in young vines even though symptoms appear years later

symptoms: A healthy grape leaf is evenly green, broad and lobed with clear veins. There are no brown, red or black spots, no striping between veins, no powdery or downy growth, and the edges are not dried or curled.
preventive: Scout the vineyard weekly, checking both leaf surfaces, young shoots and bunches
Keep the canopy open and remove diseased leaves, mummified berries and dead wood
Use only chemicals with CIB&RC label claims on grape and follow the dose and pre-harvest interval exactly
Do not repeat a pesticide that has failed; rotate chemical groups to slow resistance
Follow ICAR-NRCG weather-based advisories, especially in rainy or cloudy spells

symptoms: Large, irregular spots form on the leaves, first dull red to brown. With age the spots turn black, dry and brittle. It usually appears late in the season on vines that have not been sprayed well.

favorableConditions.rainfall: Most common late in the season in poorly protected vineyards.

organicControl: Apply Trichoderma viride/harzianum and Pseudomonas fluorescens to the cuttings/planting material and as a soil application (NIPHM grapes IPM package)

chemicalControl.activeIngredient: Fungicide for grape leaf blight (no product has a CIB&RC label claim for this disease on grape in the ICAR-NRCG 2026-27 list)
chemicalControl.dose: Consult local KVK or agriculture officer for dosage

preventive: Keep up the regular protective spray programme through the season, as advised by experts
Collect and destroy fallen infected leaves
Keep the canopy open for air movement

symptoms: Small raised chocolate-brown to brick-red powdery pustules appear on both leaf surfaces. Touching them leaves brown powder on the hand. Tissue around the pustules may turn yellow and die, and pustules turn black as they age. Badly affected leaves yellow and drop.

favorableConditions.rainfall: High humidity with cool nights (about 18-21°C) and moderate day temperatures.

chemicalControl.dose: 2.5 g per litre of water
Consult local KVK or agriculture officer for dosage

preventive: Grow resistant or tolerant varieties (NIPHM lists Buland, Sheetal, HHM 1, HHM 2, HQPM 1)
Scout leaves regularly and spray only at the first appearance of pustules
Remove crop residue and volunteer maize plants

symptoms: Long, narrow, rectangular spots (up to about 5 cm) form on the leaves, first light tan and later grey. The spots are boxed in by the leaf veins, so they have straight sides. Spots can join and kill whole leaves, starting on lower leaves a few weeks before tasselling.

favorableConditions.rainfall: Warm (about 27°C), humid weather with relative humidity above 90% for 12 hours or more; worse where maize follows maize.

chemicalControl.activeIngredient: Fungicide for grey leaf spot (no Indian dose recommendation found)
chemicalControl.dose: Consult local KVK or agriculture officer for dosage

preventive: Plant resistant hybrids
Rotate maize with non-host crops; avoid maize after maize
Reduce infected crop residue on the soil surface by tillage or residue management
Scout lower leaves from knee-high stage onwards in warm, humid weather

symptoms: A healthy maize leaf is broad, evenly green and glossy with a clear midrib. There are no long tan or grey cigar-shaped spots, no rectangular grey lesions and no brown or red powdery pustules.
preventive: Use certified seed of hybrids recommended for your region, with resistance to local diseases
Scout the lower leaves weekly, especially in humid or rainy weeks and around tasselling and silking
Rotate maize with legumes or other non-host crops
Remove or plough in crop residue after harvest
Ensure good field drainage and balanced fertilisation

commonName: Turcicum leaf blight (northern corn leaf blight)
symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped, grey-green to tan spots (2.5-15 cm) appear on the leaves, first on lower leaves and then moving upward in damp weather. In moist conditions dark grey spores make the spots look dirty. Severely affected leaves dry up completely, as if burnt.

favorableConditions.rainfall: Moist weather with long dew or rain periods keeping leaves wet for more than 6 hours; most damaging when infection occurs around silking.

chemicalControl.dose: 2.5 g per litre of water
Consult local KVK or agriculture officer for dosage

preventive: Grow resistant hybrids (NIPHM lists PEMH 5, Vivek 21, Vivek 23, Vivek 25, Pratap Kanchan 2)
Sow on time
Rotate with non-host crops such as legumes for one to two years
Destroy or plough in infected maize residue
Scout lower leaves regularly and spray at first appearance of spots

symptoms: A healthy onion leaf is a hollow, round tube standing upright out of the neck, evenly blue-green or grey-green from base to tip with a slight waxy bloom. The tip is still green and tapered, not straw-coloured or papery. There are no yellow or orange flecks in the middle of the leaf, no spindle-shaped spots with a pinkish or purple edge, no straw-coloured diamond-shaped patches, and no silvery streaks or white blotches from thrips feeding. The leaf is firm, not soft, water-soaked or collapsed, and the base of the plant is firm and white when pulled up.
preventive: Use healthy, disease-free seed or seedlings and reject thin, twisted or discoloured transplants
Walk the field weekly from 30 days after transplanting, looking at the middle of the leaf as well as the tip
Keep irrigation even; onion is sensitive to moisture stress at bulb initiation and bulb development, and to waterlogging
Follow a three-year rotation with non-host crops and remove volunteer onion plants and weeds, which carry both thrips and virus between seasons
Avoid excess nitrogen, which makes the foliage soft and more attractive to thrips

pathogen: Iris yellow spot virus (IYSV), a tospovirus spread only by onion thrips (Thrips tabaci)
symptoms: Straw-coloured, dry, tan lesions shaped like a spindle or a diamond appear on the leaf and on the seed stalk. They often have a distinct green centre, with yellow or tan borders. Unlike a fungal spot there is no mould growth on the lesion in damp weather. Severely affected leaves and seed stalks bend over and break at the lesion. Look for silvery streaks and tiny thrips in the leaf axils at the same time, because the virus only arrives with them.

favorableConditions.rainfall: Hot, dry weather, which builds thrips numbers quickly. Spread follows the vector, not leaf wetness, so it is worst in dry spells and in crops next to older onion fields, volunteer plants or weeds carrying thrips.

organicControl: Use virus-free transplants: the virus arrives with infected seedlings as often as with thrips
Three-year crop rotation, and destroy volunteer onion plants and weeds, which carry both the virus and the thrips through the off season
Sow two rows of a barrier crop such as maize or wheat around the field 30 days before transplanting, so thrips land on the barrier rather than the onion (ICAR-DOGR)
Avoid crop stress: a water-stressed or under-fed crop shows far worse symptoms
Use blue sticky traps to watch thrips numbers so sprays start at the right time rather than on a calendar

symptoms: Small dark brown to black dots appear first on the older, lower leaves. They swell into round spots about 1 mm across, then grow to roughly 5-10 mm - about the size of a small coin. symptoms: Look at the edge of the older, lower leaves first. If you cut across the leaf stalk or the top of the root, the ring of water-carrying tissue inside looks blackened. Affected plants are stunted and often lopsided because one side of the plant is hit harder, leaves get malformed, dry up and die. In warm wet weather a sticky bacterial ooze can be seen on the affected parts, and a soft, foul-smelling rot follows. Plants infected early wilt and die outright.
